{{Short description|Concept in program evaluation}}
'''Implementation fidelity''' (also called '''implementation integrity''' or '''treatment fidelity''') is a concept in [[program evaluation]] that determines the extent to which anyone using a [[research design]] is actually able to follow the [[methodology]].

A project with high fidelity is performed as designed.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Carroll |first1=Christopher |last2=Patterson |first2=Malcolm |last3=Wood |first3=Stephen |last4=Booth |first4=Andrew |last5=Rick |first5=Jo |last6=Balain |first6=Shashi |title=A conceptual framework for implementation fidelity |journal=Implementation Science |date=December 2007 |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=40 |pmc=2213686 | doi=10.1186/1748-5908-2-40|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Perepletchikova |first1=Francheska |title=On the Topic of Treatment Integrity: COMMENTARIES ON BOND ET AL. |journal=Clinical Psychology: Science and Practice |date=June 2011 |volume=18 |issue=2 |pages=148–153 |doi=10.1111/j.1468-2850.2011.01246.x|pmc=3137485 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schulte |first1=Ann C. |last2=Easton |first2=Julia E. |last3=Parker |first3=Justin |title=Advances in treatment integrity research: Multidisciplinary perspectives on the conceptualization, measurement, and enhancement of treatment integrity |journal=School Psychology Review |date=1 December 2009 |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=460–475 |url=https://asu.pure.elsevier.com/en/publications/advances-in-treatment-integrity-research-multidisciplinary-perspe |issn=0279-6015}}</ref>
